title: Multi-Source Infection Metrics
prompt:
Implement `infection_metrics(n, edges, sources) -> tuple[int, int]` for an undirected, unweighted graph whose nodes are `0` through `n - 1`. An infection begins at every distinct node in `sources` at time 0, then spreads simultaneously across one edge per time step.

Return `(time_to_reach_every_node, largest_newly_infected_wave)`. The first value is the greatest infection time when every node is reached; return `-1` when any node is unreachable from every source. The second value is the largest number of nodes first infected in one positive-time wave. Initial sources are not a wave, and the second value is `0` when no node is newly infected.

Treat repeated source IDs and repeated edges as one source or connection for infection purposes. Use a multi-source breadth-first search. The graph may be disconnected, and `sources` may be empty.

example.reasoning: Nodes 1 and 2 form the first new wave, while node 4 is first reached at time 3.
